definitions.explanation: The track-and-field event in which the athlete swings a metal ball attached to a wire handle inside a throwing circle and releases it for maximum distance. One of the four throwing events in athletics, alongside shot put, discus, and javelin.

examples.japanese: ハンマー{投|な}げ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{選手|せんしゅ}→選手：03823_senshu⟧。
⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ハンマー{投|な}げ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{金|きん}メダル→金メダル：20781_kinmedaru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}った→取る：00565_toru⟧。
examples.english: He won a gold medal in the hammer throw.

examples.japanese: ハンマー{投|な}げ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{投擲|とうてき}⟦{種目|しゅもく}→種目：27734_shumoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧。

examples.english: Athlete Koji Murofushi won the gold medal in the hammer throw at the Athens Olympics.

notes:
Composed of the loanword ⟦ハンマー→ハンマー：25887_hanmaa⟧ (hammer) and the nominalized verb stem ⟦{投|な}げ→投げ：21942_nage⟧ (throwing, from ⟦{投|な}げる→投げる：01135_nageru⟧ "to throw"). Refers only to the athletic event, not to throwing an actual hammer.

USAGE:
Used almost exclusively as the name of the sport. The person who competes is a ハンマー{投|な}げ⟦{選手|せんしゅ}→選手：03823_senshu⟧. The implement itself is called a ⟦ハンマー→ハンマー：25887_hanmaa⟧, though it is actually a metal ball on a wire.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ハンマー{投|な}げ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{選手|せんしゅ}→選手：03823_senshu⟧: hammer thrower
- ハンマー{投|な}げ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{記録|きろく}→記録：02490_kiroku⟧: hammer throw record
- ハンマー{投|な}げ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{優勝|ゆうしょう}する→優勝する：25496_yuushousuru⟧: to win the hammer throw
- ハンマー{投|な}げ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{決勝|けっしょう}→決勝：04742_kesshou⟧: the hammer throw final

RELATED EVENTS:
- ⟦{砲丸投|ほうがんな}げ→砲丸投げ：09273_hougannage⟧: shot put
- ⟦{円盤投|えんばんな}げ→円盤投げ：09274_enbannage⟧: discus throw
- ⟦やり{投|な}げ→やり投げ：22276_yarinage⟧: javelin throw

All four of these {投擲種目|とうてきしゅもく} (throwing events) follow the same {〜投|な}げ naming pattern, using a nominalized form of ⟦{投|な}げる→投げる：01135_nageru⟧.
